name: Peter Paul Rubens
findings: Uses smoky black 1.4x more than the other paintings from the same museum(s), so camera and varnish are held equal (from 1291 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, purple red turns up as a small accent in 86% of the paintings that hold it, 1.8x the archive's rate (from 1291 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, blue slate turns up as the lightest note in 70% of the paintings that hold it, 2.8x the archive's rate (from 1291 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, chocolate turns up as the shadow in 75% of the paintings that hold it, 2.2x the archive's rate (from 1291 paintings here).
Pairs battleship grey with dim grey more than chance would predict (3 of 1291 paintings here).
Pairs cocoa with mikado brown more than chance would predict (3 of 1291 paintings here).
His single largest palette family (smoky black, dark olive brown, bistre) covers 51% of his paintings here.
Keeps 2 distinct palette families here, from smoky black, dark olive brown to smoky black, black.
